accessNotes: The data-viz guidelines page is static HTML and fully readable. Its linked colour palette PDF (one large landscape page with swatches, example Power BI charts and a typography spec) was downloaded and rendered to PNG with ImageMagick. Note the PDF (Power BI oriented) specifies Arial / Times New Roman sizes that differ from the web page (Tableau Sans / Helvetica table); both are recorded. CMU Red is #c41230 on the web page and #c41330 in the PDF.
summary: University brand guideline for Tableau/Power BI reports and dashboards. Accessibility-first, plain style: one colour for all bars unless categories need distinguishing, CMU Red reserved to mark CMU against dark-grey peers, direct labels instead of legends, bold 15pt titles and Helvetica/Tableau Sans text. Example charts are flat, light-grey-gridded Power BI defaults with brand palettes.

colors.categoricalNotes: Web page: 'Categorical Core' = CMU Red #c41230 (represents CMU) + Dark Gray #4d5051 (all other values); 'Categorical Secondary' = Dark Green #1f4c4c, Highlands Sky Blue #007bc0, Weaver Blue #182c4b, Skibo Red #941120, used with the core palette. White text on all these colours. For internal audiences or financial data avoid red; use a secondary colour. PDF palettes (ordered top-to-bottom): 'Categorical CMU Basics' #043673, #a89e82, #941120, #007bc0, #1f4c4c, #719f94, #460054, #00853e; 'Categorical CMU Secondary' #007bc0, #043673, #008f91, #fdb515, #ef3a47, #00853e, #800054, #a89e82; 'Categorical Accessible Neutral - PowerBI Default' (all colours contrast above 4.5 and 3:1 for adjacent colours) #6b797c, #362b2b, #b08d72, #40484a, #86989c, #5b3d35, #928f8b, #242828; 'Categorical Bright' #0089b6, #003b76, #ef483d, #800054, #88a427, #137c76, #f7931d, #c2002f. 'CMU Highlight Against Peers': #c41330 for CMU then greys #4d5051, #6e6e6e, #919191, #b6b6b6, #dddddd for peers. Use as few colours as possible.
colors.notes: Web page: Sequential Primary = Highlands Sky Blue #007bc0 (single-hue ramp); Sequential Secondary = Gold Thread #fdb515; Divergent = Gold Thread #fdb515 to Highlands Sky Blue #007bc0. PDF Divergent (high to low): #007bc0, #8daacf, #dddddd, #e4aa79, #d87800. PDF Sentiment (positive to negative): #043673, #cdd7e3, #f1f1f1, #eacfd2, #941120. Links in Carnegie Red. Colour must never be the only means of conveying information.

typography.family: Helvetica (Tableau Sans when using Tableau; Arial in the Power BI palette PDF)

dataLabel.weight: regular (bold only for data points to call attention to)

typography.notes: Web page table (pt): section dividers 20pt regular; title 15pt bold; subtitle 13pt regular; axis labels 12pt regular; data labels 11pt regular (bold only to call attention); notes/annotations 12pt regular; links 12pt regular underlined in Carnegie Red. Pixel values above = pt x 4/3. PDF (Power BI): report titles Times New Roman 28-32pt; KPI numbers Arial Bold 24-28pt; KPI titles/headers and chart/table titles Arial Regular 14-16pt; data labels/axis captions Arial Bold 11-12pt; legends & category labels Arial Regular 9-10pt.

structure.gridlines: Example charts in the palette PDF show thin light-grey horizontal gridlines only (vertical gridlines on horizontal bar examples). Not specified in text.
structure.axisLine: Not stated; examples show no axis lines.
structure.zeroLine: Bars always start at a zero baseline; scatter plots use zero baseline on both axes.
structure.notes: Skip axis labels at regular intervals to avoid clutter.

legend.placement: avoid; when used (PDF peer example) top-centre, horizontal
legend.directLabels: Preferred: 'When possible, avoid using a legend. Instead, incorporate your data labels directly into the data visualization.'

marks.bars: One colour for all categories compared against the same measure (unless paired with other charts using colour for categories); ordinal data sorted ascending or descending; zero baseline; may be stacked for proportions.
marks.lines: PDF examples: medium lines with round point markers at each data point.
marks.points: Dot size can convey an extra variable; colour identifies patterns and outliers; trend line allowed.
marks.pies: Pie & donut best limited to 2-3 slices; stacked bar preferred for comparing percentages.
marks.notes: Heatmap: colour density for one variable. Maps: sequential palette, limit to regions in data, no decorative shading.

labels.dataLabels: Label important values/data points on the chart; white text over brand colours; bold only data points to call attention to.
labels.numberFormat: Commas as thousands separators, limit decimal places, round numbers.
labels.dates: Standard abbreviations: Sun, Mon, Tue; Jan, Feb, Mar.

furniture.title: Short but descriptive title that summarises the story the chart tells.
furniture.source: Captions, notes and summaries should concisely explain the visual; no source format specified.
furniture.other: Accompanying text summary should tell the same story on its own.

annotations: Notes/annotations 12pt regular; important data should be indicated with text in the graph, not only via hover.
layout: Limit a visualization to one main theme with two or three supporting concepts. Dashboards: presentation (high-level metrics, simple charts), operational, exploratory.
interaction: Tableau hover only for drill-down to supporting data; key messages must be visible as text for keyboard/screen-reader users.
accessibility: About 4.5% of people have colour-vision deficiency: colour cannot be the only encoding. Accessible Neutral palette: all colours contrast above 4.5:1 and 3:1 between adjacent colours. Consider screen readers, Braille keyboards and keyboard-only navigation.

chartTypes.notes: Stick to common chart types when audience data literacy is unknown.

distinctiveRules.rule: When comparing CMU to other institutions, CMU is CMU Red #c41230 and every other value is Dark Gray #4d5051 (or a ladder of greys).
distinctiveRules.quote: use CMU Red to represent CMU. Use Dark Gray to represent all other values.

distinctiveRules.rule: Data labels and marks that sit over brand colours are white.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use white text for data labels and marks that appear over these colors.

distinctiveRules.rule: Avoid red for internal audiences or financial data; use a secondary colour instead.
distinctiveRules.quote: If your visualization is directed to an internal audience, use a color from the secondary palette rather than red.

distinctiveRules.rule: Bars use a single colour for all categories against one measure, sorted ascending/descending, starting at zero.
distinctiveRules.quote: use one color to represent all categories compared against the same measure

distinctiveRules.rule: Sequential scales are single-hue Highlands Sky Blue #007bc0; diverging runs Gold Thread #fdb515 to Highlands Sky Blue #007bc0.
distinctiveRules.quote: Sequential Primary: Highlands Sky Blue #007bc0 ... Divergent: Gold Thread, Highlands Sky Blue

distinctiveRules.rule: Title 15pt bold, subtitle 13pt regular, axis labels 12pt, data labels 11pt regular, notes 12pt.
distinctiveRules.quote: Title 15pt Bold; Subtitle 13pt Regular; Axis labels 12pt; Data labels 11pt Regular

distinctiveRules.rule: Font: Tableau Sans in Tableau, Helvetica in other tools.
distinctiveRules.quote: When using Tableau, the typeface Tableau Sans should be used ... For other data visualization tools, use the typeface Helvetica.
When possible, avoid using a legend. Instead, incorporate your data labels directly

distinctiveRules.rule: Pie and donut charts limited to 2-3 slices.
Scatter plots use a zero baseline on both axes.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use a baseline of zero for the x-axis and y-axis

distinctiveRules.rule: Links in charts are 12pt regular, underlined, in Carnegie Red.
distinctiveRules.quote: Links should be displayed in Carnegie Red

distinctiveRules.rule: Sentiment scale: positive navy #043673 through #f1f1f1 neutral to negative Skibo red #941120.

referenceImages.describes: Left half of the palette PDF. Two columns of 8 square swatches with hex labels in white ('Categorical CMU Basics' navy #043673, khaki #a89e82, dark red #941120, sky blue #007bc0, dark green #1f4c4c, sage #719f94, purple #460054, green #00853e; 'Categorical CMU Secondary'). Next to each, Power BI style demo charts: line chart with round point markers and thin light-grey horizontal gridlines, tiny grey tick labels, no axis lines; horizontal stacked bars with vertical light-grey gridlines; grouped vertical bars; a variant with one coloured bar and the rest in a grey ladder; pie with outside labels; packed bubbles. Bottom: typography spec 'Report Titles: Times New Roman 28-32pt' (bold serif), 'KPI Numbers: Arial Bold 24-28pt' in grey, 'Chart/Table Titles: Arial Regular 14-16pt', 'Data Labels/Axis Captions: Arial Bold 11-12pt', 'Legends & Category Labels: Arial Regular 9-10pt'; Divergent swatches #007bc0 #8daacf #dddddd #e4aa79 #d87800 (high to low) and Sentiment #043673 #cdd7e3 #f1f1f1 #eacfd2 #941120 (positive to negative).

Right half: 'Categorical Accessible Neutral - PowerBI Default' (greys and browns #6b797c #362b2b #b08d72 #40484a #86989c #5b3d35 #928f8b #242828) and 'Categorical Bright' palettes with same demo charts; a Washington State choropleth in the blue/orange divergent palette; KPI triangle cards in pale blue/pale pink with bold numbers. 'CMU Highlight Against Peers': swatches #c41330, #4d5051, #6e6e6e, #919191, #b6b6b6, #dddddd and a grouped column chart (Jan/Feb/Mar) where the CMU bar is red and four peer bars step from dark to light grey; legend centred above the plot with circular swatches; thin light-grey horizontal gridlines; y axis 0-5,000 with comma separators; no axis lines.
